_comment: MirageOT config. Copy to config.json. CLI flags override these. Ports below are REAL service ports (add --demo to shift them +5000 for laptop testing).
_decoys_note: Pick the protocols that match the plant you are impersonating. Fewer = more believable.
_critical_points_note: Modbus addresses that, if written, are tagged as loss-of-safety (T0880) - your SIS/limit points.
_block_threshold_note: Cumulative threat score at which a source is escalated (blocked or flagged for review, per response_mode).
_response_mode_note: OT-SAFE DEFAULT. 'alert-only' = never auto-drop traffic; raise the alert and let a human decide (recommended for OT, where a wrong block can hurt availability/safety). 'blocklist' = auto-write untrusted sources to the blocklist for firewall ingestion.
_never_block_note: IPs/CIDRs that must NEVER be blocked even in blocklist mode: OT asset subnets (HMI/PLC/SCADA), engineering stations, and your own asset/vuln scanners. A hit from these still ALERTS (someone/something legit touched a decoy = investigate), but traffic is never dropped.
_syslog_note: Optional. CEF over UDP to a SIEM (FortiSIEM/Splunk/QRadar/Wazuh). Remove to disable.
_webhook_note: Optional. HIGH/CRITICAL alerts are POSTed as JSON {text:...} (Slack/Teams/SOAR compatible). Remove to disable.
